proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(c=(a,x)\).  Because \(L\ge 2\) and the values in \(\mathcal Y\) are distinct, each cell contains two indices \(u\ne w\) with \(y_u\ne y_w\).  The baseline belongs to \(\mathcal M_\eta(p)\), so \(q^0_{c\ell}\ge\eta>0\).  The variance identity
\[
 \sigma_c^2(q^0)=\sum_{\ell<m}q^0_{c\ell}q^0_{cm}(y_\ell-y_m)^2
\]
therefore gives \(\sigma_c^2(q^0)\ge\eta^2(y_u-y_w)^2>0\).  Define the cell tangent
\[
 m_{c\ell}=\frac{q^0_{c\ell}\{y_\ell-\mu_c(q^0)\}}
                         {\sigma_c^2(q^0)}.
\]
By the definitions of \(\mu_c(q^0)\) and \(\sigma_c^2(q^0)\),
\[
 \sum_{\ell=1}^L m_{c\ell}=0,
 \qquad
 \sum_{\ell=1}^L y_\ell m_{c\ell}=1.
\tag{1}
\]
Thus the cellwise restriction of \(B_{\mathrm{mean}}\) to the simplex tangent is onto \(\mathbb R\), including when \(L=2\).  Since \(\operatorname{rank}(F)=d\) by \(\mathrm{ass:menu\text{-}rank}\), \(A_{\mathrm{map}}=[-F\;F]\) has row rank \(d\).  Applying the cellwise right inverses in (1) shows that \(A_{\mathrm{tan}}=A_{\mathrm{map}}B_{\mathrm{mean}}\) is onto, consistently with the stipulated maps \(S_0\) and \(W\).

Fix \(C_v<\infty\).  The set
\(\mathcal H\times\{v:\lVert v\rVert\le C_v\}\) is compact, because \(\mathcal H\) is compact and the second factor is a closed bounded subset of a finite-dimensional space.  The map \((h,v)\mapsto S_0h+Wv\) is continuous.  Hence
\[
 C_s(C_v):=\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
             \lVert S_0h+Wv\rVert_\infty<\infty.
\tag{2}
\]
If \(n>\{C_s(C_v)/\delta_q\}^2\), then for every coordinate and every point of this compact parameter set,
\[
 q_{n,ax\ell}(h,v)
 =q^0_{ax\ell}+\frac{s(h,v)_{ax\ell}}{\sqrt n}
 \ge q^0_{ax\ell}-\frac{C_s(C_v)}{\sqrt n}
 >q^0_{ax\ell}-\delta_q\ge\eta.
\tag{3}
\]
Both \(S_0h\) and \(Wv\) lie in \(\mathcal E\), so each cell of \(s(h,v)\) sums to zero.  Consequently every cell of \(q_n(h,v)\) sums to one.  Equation (3), \(\mathrm{def:saturated\text{-}model}\), and its randomization and consistency member properties yield
\[
 q_n(h,v)\in(\Delta_{L-1})^{2K},
 \qquad P_{p,q_n(h,v)}\in\mathcal M_\eta(p),
\tag{4}
\]
uniformly on the stated domain.

The cell means are linear in \(q\).  Using \(A_{\mathrm{tan}}S_0=I_d\), \(A_{\mathrm{tan}}W=0\), and \(\mathrm{ass:tied\text{-}baseline}\), we obtain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sqrt n\,\theta_p(q_n(h,v))
 &=\sqrt n\,\theta_p(q^0)+A_{\mathrm{map}}B_{\mathrm{mean}}s(h,v)\\
 &=A_{\mathrm{tan}}S_0h+A_{\mathrm{tan}}Wv=h.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]

It remains to establish exact nuisance coverage.  For each cell, every \(s_c\) in its simplex tangent has the unique decomposition
\[
 s_c=m_c b_c+k_c,
 \qquad b_c=\sum_{\ell=1}^L y_\ell s_{c\ell},
 \qquad
 \sum_{\ell=1}^L k_{c\ell}=sum_{\ell=1}^L y_\ell k_{c\ell}=0,
\tag{6}
\]
where (1) proves existence and uniqueness.  The cellwise shape space in (6) has dimension \(L-2\): the sum and mean functionals are linearly independent because the support contains two distinct values.  In particular, that dimension is zero when \(L=2\).

Let \(h\in\mathcal H\), let \(u\in\mathbb R^{K-d}\), let \(c\in\mathbb R^K\) be an arbitrary common-arm-mean direction, and choose arbitrary cellwise shape vectors \(k_{ax}\) satisfying the two equalities in (6).  Set
\[
 b_0=c,
 \qquad b_1=c+Qh+Nu,
 \qquad s^*_{ax}=m_{ax}b_{ax}+k_{ax}.
\tag{7}
\]
Equations (1) and (6) give \(B_{\mathrm{mean}}s^*=b\).  Since \(FQ=I_d\) and \(FN=0\),
\[
 A_{\mathrm{tan}}s^*=A_{\mathrm{map}}b
 =F(b_1-b_0)=F(Qh+Nu)=h.
\tag{8}
\]
Therefore \(s^*-S_0h\in\ker(A_{\mathrm{tan}})=\operatorname{im}(W)\).  The bijectivity of \(W\) supplies the unique coordinate
\[
 v=W^{-1}(s^*-S_0h).
\tag{9}
\]
All maps in (7)--(9) are linear between finite-dimensional spaces, so bounded sets of \((h,u,c,k)\) map to bounded sets of \(v\).  In particular, taking \(c=0\) and \(k=0\) proves the claimed realization of every bounded treatment-effect direction \(Qh+Nu\); varying \(c\) and \(k\) independently gives every common-arm-mean and zero-mean outcome-shape direction.

Finally, these nuisance coordinates exhaust rather than merely embed in the kernel.  Their dimensions are
\[
 K+(K-d)+2K(L-2)=2K(L-1)-d=\dim\ker(A_{\mathrm{tan}}),
\tag{10}
\]
where the last equality uses surjectivity of \(A_{\mathrm{tan}}\).  The decomposition (6) and the direct decomposition \(b_0=c\), \(b_1=c+Nu\) of \(\ker(A_{\mathrm{map}})\) show that the sum in (10) is direct.  This proves full coverage also at the binary-support endpoint \(L=2\).

Fix \(C_v<\infty\), and write \(c_{ax}=p_xe_{ax}\).  The stipulated spaces of \(p\) and \(e\) imply \(c_{ax}>0\) in each of the finitely many cells.  Because \(L\ge2\) and the support values are distinct, choose \(y_u\ne y_w\).  For any probability vector \(q_{ax}\), expansion around its mean gives
\[
 \sigma^2_{ax}(q)=\sum_{\ell<m}q_{ax\ell}q_{axm}(y_\ell-y_m)^2.
\tag{11}
\]
Since \(q^0_{ax\ell}\ge\eta\) by \(\mathrm{ass:eta\text{-}interior}\),
\[
 \underline\sigma^2:=\eta^2(y_u-y_w)^2
 \le\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)\le4C_Y^2.
\tag{12}
\]
Thus two support points, and not a third, are sufficient for the positive variance floor.

For \(z\in\mathbb R^d\), the covariance definition gives
\[
 z^\top\Sigma(r)z
 =\sum_{x=1}^K\sum_{a=0}^1
   \frac{p_x\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)}{e_{ax}r_{ax}}(z^\top d_x)^2.
\tag{13}
\]
The coefficients in (13) have fixed positive lower and finite upper bounds because \(r_{ax}\in[\rho,1]\), \(p_x,e_{ax}>0\), and (12) holds.  Moreover \(\operatorname{rank}(F)=d\), and \(F=[d_1\;\cdots\;d_K]\operatorname{diag}(p)\) with positive diagonal \(\operatorname{diag}(p)\), so \(d_1,\ldots,d_K\) span \(\mathbb R^d\).  Hence \(z\mapsto\sum_x(z^\top d_x)^2\) has a positive minimum on the unit sphere.  Equation (13) places
\[
 \{\Sigma(r):r\in\mathcal R_B\}
\quad\text{in a fixed compact set}\quad
 \mathcal K\subset\mathbb S_{++}^d.
\tag{14}
\]

We next build a uniformly accurate pilot objective under the two stipulated pilot limits.  Put
\[
 b_n=m_n^{-1/4}+n^{-1/2},
 \qquad t_n=b_n^{1/2}.
\tag{15}
\]
The assumption \(m_n\to\infty\) gives \(b_n\to0\), \(t_n\to0\), and
\[
 b_n/t_n=b_n^{1/2}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{16}
\]
Let \(N_{ax}\) count fully labelled pilot records in cell \((a,x)\).  For \(s\in\{1,2\}\), let \(\widehat\nu_{s,ax}\) be the within-cell mean of \(Y^s\), with any value in the bounded range when \(N_{ax}=0\), and write
\(\nu_{s,ax,n}=E_{q_n(h,v)}(Y^s\mid A=a,X=x)\).  Uniformly in \(h\in\mathcal H\) and \(\lVert v\rVert\le C_v\), boundedness of \(Y\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\!\left(\frac{N_{ax}}{m_n}\right)
 \le\frac{c_{ax}}{m_n},
 \qquad
 E\!\left[
 \left\{\frac1{m_n}\sum_{i=1}^{m_n}
 \mathbf1\{X_i=x,A_i=a\}(Y_i^s-\nu_{s,ax,n})\right\}^2
 \right]
 \le\frac{c_{ax}(2C_Y^s)^2}{m_n}.
\tag{17}
\]
Chebyshev's inequality first yields
\(P(N_{ax}<m_nc_{ax}/2)=O(m_n^{-1})\).  On the complementary event, division by \(N_{ax}/m_n\ge c_{ax}/2\) in the second display in (17), followed again by Chebyshev at threshold \(m_n^{-1/4}\), yields constants \(C_{ax,s}\) such that
\[
 \sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
 P_{q_n(h,v)}\!left(
 |\widehat\nu_{s,ax}-\nu_{s,ax,n}|>C_{ax,s}m_n^{-1/4}
 \right)=O(m_n^{-1/2}).
\tag{18}
\]
The constants are uniform because only the fixed cell probabilities and the bound on \(Y\) enter.  A union bound over the fixed \(4K\) coordinates supplies events \(E_n(C_v)\) satisfying
\[
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H,\,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
 P_{q_n(h,v)}\{E_n(C_v)\}\longrightarrow1.
\tag{19}
\]

Continuity of \((h,v)\mapsto S_0h+Wv\) on the compact bounded-fiber domain gives a finite uniform bound on \(\lVert s(h,v)\rVert_\infty\).  Since \(q_n-q^0=s(h,v)/\sqrt n\) and the support is finite,
\[
 \max_{a,x,\,s\in\{1,2\}}
 |\nu_{s,ax,n}-\nu_{s,ax,0}|\le C(C_v)n^{-1/2}.
\tag{20}
\]
The map \((\nu_1,\nu_2)\mapsto\nu_2-\nu_1^2\) is Lipschitz on the bounded moment rectangle.  Clip the resulting pilot variance estimates to \([\underline\sigma^2/2,4C_Y^2]\).  Equations (18)--(20) imply on \(E_n(C_v)\)
\[
 \max_{a,x}|\widehat\sigma^2_{ax}-\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)|
 \le C_0(C_v)b_n.
\tag{21}
\]
No comparison between \(m_n\) and \(\sqrt n\) was used.

Let \(\widehat\Sigma_n(r)\) replace the cell variances in \(\Sigma(r)\) by the clipped pilot estimates, and let \(\widehat L_n(r)\) be the corresponding Gaussian minimax value.  Since \(r_{ax}\ge\rho\), (21) gives
\[
 \sup_{r\in\mathcal R_B}
 \lVert\widehat\Sigma_n(r)-\Sigma(r)\rVert
 \le C_1(C_v)b_n.
\tag{22}
\]
For positive-definite matrices \(S,S'\) in a sufficiently small compact enlargement of \(\mathcal K\), set \(S_t=(1-t)S+tS'\).  Differentiation of the centered normal density gives
\[
 \frac{d}{dt}\phi_{S_t}(z)
 =\frac12\phi_{S_t}(z)
 \left[z^\top S_t^{-1}(S'-S)S_t^{-1}z
       -\operatorname{tr}\{S_t^{-1}(S'-S)\}\right].
\tag{23}
\]
The common eigenvalue bounds from (14), integration in \(z\) and \(t\), and translation invariance imply
\[
 \sup_{h\in\mathbb R^d}
 \operatorname{TV}\{N(h,S),N(h,S')\}
 \le C_2\lVert S-S'\rVert.
\tag{24}
\]
The regret is bounded by
\(R_H=2\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}\lVert h\rVert_\infty<\infty\).  Thus changing \(S\) to \(S'\) changes the risk of every rule at every state by at most \(R_H\) times (24).  Taking successively the supremum over states and the infimum over rules, in both directions, yields from (22)
\[
 \sup_{r\in\mathcal R_B}|\widehat L_n(r)-L(r)|
 \le C_3(C_v)b_n
 \quad\text{on }E_n(C_v).
\tag{25}
\]

We now construct the nested-cell selector.  Set
\(k_n=\max\{0,\lfloor\log_2\log(n+2)\rfloor\}\).  Through depth \(k_n\), use precisely the coordinate order, parent-only recursion, closed-child convention, and lexicographic order in \(\mathrm{def:implementation\text{-}handle}\).  On every nonempty feasible part of a child of the currently selected parent, approximate the minimum of \(\widehat L_n\) with deterministic error at most \(b_n\).

Such finite approximations exist uniformly.  Indeed, \(P_B\) is continuous and equals the identity on \(\mathcal R_B\), so projecting refining ambient finite nets through \(P_B\) gives dense finite nets in \(\mathcal R_B\).  If \(C=\mathcal R_B\cap D\) is a nonempty closed child cell, project each such point \(g\) onto the compact convex set \(C\).  The nearest point \(c_C(g)\) exists and is unique; if \(c\in C\) and \(\lVert g-c\rVert\le\xi\), then
\[
 \lVert c_C(g)-c\rVert
 \le\lVert c_C(g)-g\rVert+\lVert g-c\rVert\le2\xi.
\tag{26}
\]
Thus the cellwise nets refine even for singleton cells and cells contained in a dyadic boundary.  On represented inputs, \(\mathrm{thm:certified\text{-}computation}\), after adding the child's rational box inequalities, supplies terminating outward certificates.  For a fixed mathematical instance, deterministic simple-function refinement gives the same approximation without an effectiveness assertion.

For completeness, the Gaussian-game approximation is uniform.  Differentiating a Gaussian density in its mean as in (23) gives, uniformly for \(S\in\mathcal K\),
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\{N(h,S),N(h',S)\}\le C_5\lVert h-h'\rVert.
\tag{27}
\]
The loss is uniformly Lipschitz in \(h\), so every rule's risk has a common modulus on compact \(\mathcal H\).  A finite state net therefore approximates all worst-state risks uniformly.  For finite state and covariance nets, let \(\mu\) be the sum of the finitely many Gaussian laws.  Rational rectangles generate the Borel sigma-field; consequently every measurable simplex-valued rule admits rectangle-simple component approximations in \(L^1(\mu)\).  Projection of their values onto \(\Delta_M\) preserves measurability and convergence.  A covariance net and (24) make the approximation uniform over \(\mathcal K\).  Taking a rule arbitrarily close to the defining infimum proves convergence of the finite rectangle games to the Gaussian games.  All finite-stage operations are Borel functions of the pilot moments, and lexicographic resolution of finitely many comparisons makes the design selector jointly measurable.

Let \(\widehat v_{n,j,b}\) denote the approximate value of feasible child \(b\) at depth \(j\).  When the parent is the population box \(\mathcal D_{j-1}^\dagger\), put
\[
 v_{j,b}=\min_{r\in\mathcal R_B\cap D_{j,b}}L(r).
\]
Combining (25) with the numerical tolerance gives a deterministic
\(\alpha_n=C_4(C_v)b_n\) such that, on \(E_n(C_v)\),
\[
 |\widehat v_{n,j,b}-v_{j,b}|\le\alpha_n
\tag{28}
\]
simultaneously for all children tested through depth \(k_n\).  By (16), \(\alpha_n=o(t_n)\).  Retain exactly the siblings satisfying
\[
 \widehat v_{n,j,b}\le\min_c\widehat v_{n,j,c}+t_n,
\tag{29}
\]
and choose the lexicographically first retained child.  The sibling attaining the finite approximate minimum is retained, so the empirical cell is nonempty; parent-only recursion makes the empirical cells nested.

For the feasible children of \(\mathcal D_{j-1}^\dagger\), define
\[
 E_j=\{b:v_{j,b}=V^*\},
 \qquad
 \gamma_j(L)=
 \begin{cases}
 \min_{b\notin E_j}(v_{j,b}-V^*),&
 E_j\text{ is not all feasible children},\\
 +\infty,&E_j\text{ is all feasible children}.
 \end{cases}
\tag{30}
\]
At least one child belongs to \(E_j\), because the finitely many closed children cover the selected compact parent cell, which contains a minimizer.  Continuity of \(L\), itself a consequence of the covariance formula and (24), makes every child minimum attained.  Hence every child outside \(E_j\) has value strictly larger than \(V^*\), and finiteness gives \(\gamma_j(L)>0\).

Assume inductively that the empirical parent at depth \(j-1\) equals \(\mathcal D_{j-1}^\dagger\).  Under (28), every child in \(E_j\) is retained whenever \(2\alpha_n<t_n\), while every child outside \(E_j\) is rejected whenever
\[
 t_n+2\alpha_n<\gamma_j(L).
\tag{31}
\]
Under these inequalities the retained children are exactly \(E_j\), and their lexicographically first member is \(\mathcal D_j^\dagger\).  Induction proves stabilization of every fixed prefix.  If a minimizer lies on a shared dyadic boundary, every closed child containing it is separately feasible and lies in \(E_j\); all are retained before the same lexicographic rule is applied.  Disconnected, flat, or separated tied minimizing sets only enlarge \(E_j\).  Thus (28)--(31) cover both separated ties and dyadic-boundary minima.

The outward cell bounds from \(\mathrm{thm:certified\text{-}computation}\), or deterministic convergent bounds for a fixed instance, eventually certify a positive lower bound for each finite positive gap in (30).  Let \(j_n(L)\le k_n\) be the largest certified depth for which the approximation envelope is smaller than all positive prefix gaps through that depth, with \(j_n(L)=0\) if there is no such level.  This is an analysis sequence depending on the pilot schedule and the population prefix-separation profile, not on \(C_v\).  For every fixed depth, (16), (28), and positivity of the finitely many preceding gaps eventually imply (31).  Since \(k_n\to\infty\),
\[
 j_n(L)\longrightarrow\infty,
 \qquad
 a_n(L):=\sup_{m\ge n}2^{-j_m(L)}\downarrow0.
\tag{32}
\]
Choose a point from the final selected compact feasible cell by successively minimizing its coordinates; this fixed rule is Borel measurable on the countable family of cells.  On \(E_n(C_v)\), both that point \(\widehat r_n\) and \(r^\dagger\) belong to the same depth-\(j_n(L)\) population cell.  The dyadic diameter bound gives
\[
 \lVert\widehat r_n-r^\dagger\rVert
 \le\sqrt{2K}(1-\rho)2^{-j_n(L)}
 \le\sqrt{2K}(1-\rho)a_n(L).
\tag{33}
\]
Equations (19), (32), and (33) establish local uniform convergence in probability and
\(\lVert\widehat r_n-r^\dagger\rVert=O_P\{a_n(L)\}\).  The rate is necessarily schedule- and law-specific through (15) and the gaps (30).

It remains to couple the selector to the terminal Gaussian rule.  At deterministic refinement level \(s\), use \(\widehat\Sigma_n(\widehat r_n)\), a finite state net, and a rational observation-rectangle partition after tail truncation, and solve the finite Gaussian game to total error at most \(2^{-s}\), resolving finite ties lexicographically.  Let \(J_s<\infty\) be the number of rectangles.  A diagonal choice \(s_n\uparrow\infty\) can be made slowly enough that
\[
 J_{s_n}n^{-1/2}\longrightarrow0,
\tag{34}
\]
while the state-mesh, tail, quadrature, rounding, covariance, and finite-game errors vanish.  Each level uses only finitely many Borel pilot statistics and comparisons, so the rectangle rule is jointly measurable with \(\widehat r_n\).

To verify its distributional coupling, put \(\beta_n=\beta(q_n(h,v))\), \(b=\beta_n-\widehat\beta\), and, conditionally on \(\mathscr P_n\), define
\[
 H_{i,ax}=
 \frac{\mathbf1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,R_i=1\}}
 {p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
 (Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat\beta_{ax}).
\tag{35}
\]
Annotation ignorability gives \(E(H_i\mid\mathscr P_n)=b\).  The conditional summands \(A_{\mathrm{map}}(H_i-b)\) are centered and uniformly bounded because \(Y\) and the clipped pilot means are bounded, \(p_xe_{ax}>0\), and \(\widehat r_{n,ax}\ge\rho\).  Only one coordinate of \(H_i\) can be nonzero, so their exact conditional covariance is
\[
 S_n=A_{\mathrm{map}}\left[
 \operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
 \frac{\sigma^2_{ax}(q_n)+b_{ax}^2}
 {p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
 \right\}-bb^\top\right]A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top.
\tag{36}
\]
The bracketed \(b\)-remainder is itself a covariance matrix and is positive semidefinite.  The same bounded-cell second-moment argument as in (17) gives, locally uniformly,
\[
 \lVert b\rVert=O_P(m_n^{-1/2}).
\tag{37}
\]
The affine local chart gives
\[
 \max_{a,x}|\sigma^2_{ax}(q_n)-\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)|=O(n^{-1/2})
\tag{38}
\]
uniformly on the bounded fiber.  The \((0,x)\) and \((1,x)\) columns of \(A_{\mathrm{map}}\) are \(-p_xd_x\) and \(p_xd_x\), respectively, and therefore
\[
 A_{\mathrm{map}}\operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
 \frac{\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)}{p_xe_{ax}r_{ax}}
 \right\}A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top=\Sigma(r).
\tag{39}
\]
Equations (33), (36)--(39), and continuity of reciprocal rates on \([\rho,1]\) imply
\[
 \lVert S_n-\Sigma(r^\dagger)\rVert
 =O_P\{m_n^{-1}+n^{-1/2}+a_n(L)\}=o_P(1)
\tag{40}
\]
locally uniformly.  This covariance step needs only \(m_n\to\infty\).

By (12)--(14), (38), and (40), \(S_n\) has a common positive lower eigenvalue with probability tending to one uniformly on the bounded fiber.  Normalize the \(n\) summands in the exact identity
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_p(q_n(h,v))\}
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^nA_{\mathrm{map}}(H_i-b)
\tag{41}
\]
by \(S_n^{-1/2}\).  Uniform boundedness makes the sum of the third absolute Euclidean moments of the normalized scaled summands \(O(n^{-1/2})\).  The frozen \(\mathrm{lem:bentkus\text{-}convex\text{-}set}\) therefore bounds the conditional probability error of every observation rectangle by \(O(n^{-1/2})\).  Summing over the \(J_{s_n}\) rectangles and using (34), then applying (24) and (40), yields
\[
 \sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
 |\operatorname{Risk}_n(h,v)-\operatorname{Risk}_{G,n}(h,v)|=o(1).
\tag{42}
\]
The Gaussian comparison has mean \(h\), as given by the local mean identity in the established \(\mathrm{thm:nuisance\text{-}uniform\text{-}experiment}\), and covariance \(\Sigma(r^\dagger)\).  Bounded regret turns the locally uniform conditional convergence in probability into unconditional convergence.  The separate condition \(m_n/n\to0\) in \(\mathrm{ass:pilot\text{-}vanishes}\) makes the pilot likelihood negligible in that established experiment theorem.  This proves the claimed jointly refined Gaussian-rule risk coupling for every \(L\ge2\).

Finally, the rate limitation is purely generic.  For \(\epsilon>0\), define on \([0,1]\)
\[
 f_+(z)=\epsilon z,
 \qquad f_-(z)=\epsilon(1-z),
 \qquad g(z)=\epsilon/2.
\tag{43}
\]
The canonical minimizers of \(f_+\) and \(f_-\) are zero and one, whereas
\[
 \lVert g-f_+\rVert_\infty=\lVert g-f_-\rVert_\infty=\epsilon/2.
\tag{44}
\]
Any selector seeing the common approximation \(g\) returns the same \(z_g\) in both cases, and
\[
 \max\{|z_g|,|z_g-1|\}\ge\tfrac12.
\tag{45}
\]
Letting \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) rules out a spatial recovery modulus uniform over all continuous objectives when only continuity and uniform objective error are controlled.  Since (43) is not claimed to belong to the Gaussian-risk family \(r\mapsto L(r)\), no model-specific impossibility is asserted.

Use the jointly measurable construction in \(\mathrm{thm:coupled\text{-}measurable\text{-}attainment}\): fully label the independent pilot, select \(\widehat r_n\in\mathcal R_B\), acquire each main-wave outcome independently at its selected cell rate, compute \(\widetilde\theta_n\), and apply the coupled rectangle-constant Gaussian rule to \(\sqrt n\,\widetilde\theta_n\).  The design belongs to \(\mathcal R_B\) sample by sample.  The assumption \(m_n\to\infty\) is sufficient for the pilot moments and design selector, while \(m_n/n\to0\) makes the pilot information negligible in \(\mathrm{thm:nuisance\text{-}uniform\text{-}experiment}\).  Together with \(\widehat r_n\to r^\dagger\), these facts put the constructed sequence \(\mathcal A^*\) in \(\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{det}}\).  The stipulated coordinate order, parent-only recursion, separate testing of boundary-sharing closed children, stabilization of every fixed prefix, and the rate \(O_P\{a_n(L)\}\) follow from the coupled theorem.

We verify the estimator limit explicitly.  Fix \(C_v<\infty\), and condition on \(\mathscr P_n\).  Put
\[
 c_{ax}=p_xe_{ax},
 \qquad \beta_n=\beta(q_n(h,v)),
 \qquad b=\beta_n-\widehat\beta,
\]
and define
\[
 H_{i,ax}=
 \frac{\mathbf1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,R_i=1\}}
 {c_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
 (Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat\beta_{ax}).
\tag{46}
\]
Randomization and consistency identify the observed conditional outcome mean with \(\beta_{n,ax}\).  Annotation ignorability and the Bernoulli annotation probability give
\[
 E(H_{i,ax}\mid\mathscr P_n)
 =\frac{c_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
 {c_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
 (\beta_{n,ax}-\widehat\beta_{ax})=b_{ax}.
\tag{47}
\]
The definitions of \(\widetilde\beta_n\), \(\widetilde\theta_n\), and \(\theta_p\) then give the exact identities
\[
 E(\widetilde\beta_n\mid\mathscr P_n)=\beta_n,
 \qquad
 \sqrt n\{\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_p(q_n(h,v))\}
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^nA_{\mathrm{map}}(H_i-b).
\tag{48}
\]

Only one coordinate of \(H_i\) can be nonzero.  Computing its conditional second moment and using (47) gives the exact covariance
\[
 S_n=A_{\mathrm{map}}\left[
 \operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
 \frac{\sigma^2_{ax}(q_n(h,v))+b_{ax}^2}
 {p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
 \right\}-bb^\top\right]A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top.
\tag{49}
\]
The part
\[
 \operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
 \frac{b_{ax}^2}{p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
 \right\}-bb^\top
\tag{50}
\]
is positive semidefinite because it is the covariance of the vector whose \((a,x)\)-coordinate is
\(b_{ax}\mathbf1\{X=x,A=a,R=1\}/(p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax})\).

The pilot observations are bounded, there are finitely many cells, and every \(p_xe_{ax}\) is positive.  The same conditional second-moment and empty-cell calculation used in the coupled theorem gives
\[
 \lVert b\rVert=O_P(m_n^{-1/2})
\tag{51}
\]
locally uniformly on the bounded fiber.  Since \(q_n-q^0=s(h,v)/\sqrt n\), finite support and boundedness of \(s(h,v)\) yield
\[
 \max_{a,x}|\sigma^2_{ax}(q_n(h,v))-\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)|
 =O(n^{-1/2})
\tag{52}
\]
uniformly on that fiber.  The columns of \(A_{\mathrm{map}}=[-F\;F]\) corresponding to \((0,x)\) and \((1,x)\) are \(-p_xd_x\) and \(p_xd_x\).  Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &A_{\mathrm{map}}\operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
 \frac{\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)}{p_xe_{ax}r_{ax}}
 \right\}A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top\\
 &\qquad=\sum_{x=1}^K\sum_{a=0}^1
 \frac{p_x\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)}{e_{ax}r_{ax}}d_xd_x^\top
 =\Sigma(r).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{53}
\]
The fixed lower bounds on \(p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}\), equations (49)--(53), and \(\widehat r_n\to r^\dagger\) imply
\[
 \lVert S_n-\Sigma(r^\dagger)\rVert
 =O_P(m_n^{-1}+n^{-1/2})+o_P(1)=o_P(1).
\tag{54}
\]
Thus only \(m_n\to\infty\), rather than a polynomial pilot rate, is used in the covariance remainder.

Because \(L\ge2\), choose two distinct support values.  Identity (11), \(q^0_{ax\ell}\ge\eta\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(F)=d\) give a common positive eigenvalue lower bound for \(\Sigma(r)\), uniformly over \(r\in\mathcal R_B\).  Equations (52)--(54) transfer that lower bound to \(S_n\) with probability tending to one locally uniformly.  The summands in (48) are uniformly bounded because \(|Y|\le C_Y\), \(\widehat\beta\) is clipped to the convex hull of \(\mathcal Y\), \(\widehat r_{n,ax}\ge\rho\), and \(p_xe_{ax}>0\).  After multiplication by \(S_n^{-1/2}\), the sum of third Euclidean absolute moments of the \(n\) scaled summands is \(O(n^{-1/2})\).  Applying \(\mathrm{lem:bentkus\text{-}convex\text{-}set}\), followed by (54), gives
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_p(q_n(h,v))\}
 \Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma(r^\dagger))
\tag{55}
\]
uniformly over \(h\in\mathcal H\) and \(\lVert v\rVert\le C_v\).  This argument uses only the two-distinct-value variance floor and therefore covers binary outcomes.

The revalidated \(\mathrm{thm:local\text{-}chart\text{-}membership}\) gives \(\sqrt n\,\theta_p(q_n(h,v))=h\).  Hence the input \(\sqrt n\,\widetilde\theta_n\) converges to \(N(h,\Sigma(r^\dagger))\).  The coupled theorem chooses its rectangle count \(J_{s_n}\) so that \(J_{s_n}/\sqrt n\to0\); consequently the Bentkus error summed over the rectangles is \(o(1)\).  Its state-mesh, tail, quadrature, rounding, covariance, and finite-game errors also vanish.  Since \(r^\dagger\) is a minimizer of \(L\),
\[
 L(r^\dagger)=V^*,
\]
and the risk coupling yields
\[
 \sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
 E_{P_{p,q_n(h,v)},\mathcal A^*}
 [\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h,J_n(\mathcal A^*))]
 \le V^*+o(1).
\tag{56}
\]
The loss is bounded by \(2\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}\lVert h\rVert_\infty\), so conditional errors converging in probability can be integrated.  Taking \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}\) in (56) for fixed \(C_v\), then taking \(C_v\to\infty\), proves
\[
 \mathcal R_+(\mathcal A^*)\le V^*.
\tag{57}
\]
The established \(\mathrm{thm:local\text{-}minimax\text{-}lower\text{-}bound}\) gives \(\mathcal R_-(\mathcal A)\ge V^*\) for every \(\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{det}}\).  Since \(\mathcal R_-(\mathcal A^*)\le\mathcal R_+(\mathcal A^*)\), (57) proves that both deterministic-limit local minimax envelopes equal \(V^*\).

proposed_core_edits.name: \(L\)

proposed.name: \(L\)
proposed.def: Known fixed number of outcome-support points.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Two distinct support values suffice for positive cell variance and surjectivity of the cellwise mean-tangent map; at the binary endpoint the zero-mean shape subspace has dimension zero.

prose_updates.tldr: A frozen menu of overlapping policies turns prospective randomized outcome annotation into a joint decision problem because one acquired treatment--stratum outcome informs several correlated policy contrasts. The kernel covers every known fixed finite outcome support of size \(L\ge2\), including binary outcomes; it derives the conditional finite-coordinate LAN experiment uniformly over the saturated outcome model and every contrast-preserving nuisance, characterizes the deterministic-design minimax regret value \(V^*\), gives certified computation on effectively represented inputs, and constructs a measurable nested-cell selector, joint AIPW estimator, and refined Gaussian rule attaining that value at tied, flat, disconnected, or dyadic-boundary design optima. The fully labelled pilot may diverge arbitrarily slowly provided its share vanishes: \(m_n\to\infty\) gives finite-cell moment consistency and \(m_n/n\to0\) makes its local information negligible. The selector's spatial convergence rate remains schedule- and law-specific through the positive prefix gaps. A generic continuous-objective witness shows only that continuity plus uniform objective approximation cannot yield an objective-uniform spatial recovery modulus; it is not a model-specific impossibility theorem for the Gaussian-risk family. A rational three-policy, three-support-point witness establishes that minimizing a scalar maximum pairwise-variance summary does not determine the Gaussian minimax-regret-optimal design: the unique optimizer of the pairwise-variance probe has regret above \(0.1965\), while a projected feasible competitor is below \(0.18453\), with separation on an explicit open neighborhood.

project_justification.fill: The project fills the niche for known fixed finite supports of every size \(L\ge2\), including binary outcomes, with a nuisance-uniform Gaussian experiment, an exact deterministic-design minimax characterization, an effective certified solver, and a measurable tie-stable implementation requiring only \(m_n\to\infty\) and \(m_n/n\to0\). Its joint AIPW and Gaussian-rule construction attains the minimax value, while its spatial selector rate is stated honestly as schedule- and law-specific through the certified prefix-separation profile.

sampling_model.units: Independent main-wave records \(O=(X,A,R,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\) have observed law \(\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q}\), where \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y\) if \(R=1\) and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=\star\) otherwise, with fixed finite stratum space \([K]\), binary randomized treatment, and a known fixed finite outcome support \(\mathcal Y\) of size \(L\ge2\), including binary outcomes.

prose_updates.related_work: Hirano and Porter (2009) inform the scalar fixed-experiment Gaussian decision bridge, while Masten (2023) and Kato (2026) inform finite-action Gaussian games; none observes overlapping policy loadings through selectively annotated treatment--stratum cells. The general theory here applies to a known fixed finite support of every size \(L\ge2\), including binary outcomes. Higbee (2026) proves two-wave Bayes design under a unique, strongly concave smooth policy optimum. Theorem 4 gives the theorem-level contrast required here: its rational \(L=3\) finite-menu specialization has a three-way tie in every local decision neighborhood and fourteen contrast-preserving selective-annotation nuisance coordinates, so Higbee's uniqueness and curvature conditions do not cover that experiment. Nwankwo, Goldkind, and Zhou (2026) supply the closest scalar annotation workflow, and the Wang, Wang, and Miao preprint, listed as a FUTURE Statistica Sinica article, supplies the nearest componentwise semiparametric two-phase criterion. Levis et al. (2024) inform observed-data influence projection, Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas (2024) inform stabilized AIPW limits, and Luedtke and van der Laan (2016) identify the nonregularity of nonunique optimal decisions. Those works do not establish the present coupling of a tie-stable multivariate regret design and a discontinuous finite-policy rule under only an arbitrarily slowly diverging pilot and a vanishing pilot share; the resulting spatial rate is deliberately schedule- and law-specific. Manski (2007) studies minimax-regret treatment choice when outcomes are missing for uncontrolled reasons and the response law is partially identified. Stoye (2007) extends incomplete-data choice to many treatments, and his finite-sample missing-outcome analysis studies a fixed exogenous missing fraction. Those decision problems are important antecedents but differ from prospective randomized annotation, known propensities, point-identified policy contrasts, and optimization of the acquisition design itself. Hu et al. (2024) inform regret-sensitive allocation in separable subgroup decisions. The auxiliary functional \(G_\omega\) is introduced internally only as the geometric probe in the constructive \(L=3\) witness. Codi et al. (2025) provide the stacked rule-comparison consumer, and Kim et al. (2025) motivate independent validation of the azithromycin rules. Continuous-outcome extensions remain outside the fixed-support formulation.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The comparison class contains procedures whose fully labelled pilot sizes satisfy \(m_n\to\infty\) and \(m_n/n\to0\), and whose main-wave annotation rates converge to a deterministic feasible design; no polynomial pilot-growth condition is imposed. Fully sequential acquisition, positive-fraction pilots, bounded pilots, and random limiting designs are different experiments. The known fixed finite support has size \(L\ge2\) and uniformly positive cell probabilities, so binary outcomes are included; continuously supported outcomes require a separate support formulation. Certified computation is asserted only for rational-polytopal state sets and rational or real-algebraic encoded inputs with exact certificates; no algorithmic claim covers arbitrary opaque reals or oracle-free compact sets. The certificate returns value bounds and an outer minimizer cover, while the measurable selector has a schedule- and law-specific spatial rate determined by its pilot envelope and certified prefix gaps. The generic continuous-objective counterexample rules out a recovery modulus based only on continuity and uniform objective error; it does not establish a model-specific rate impossibility for the Gaussian-risk family. The auxiliary pairwise-variance functional \(G_\omega\) is used solely as the geometric probe in the rational \(L=3\) witness. The \(M=2\) proposition recovers the known Blackwell-monotone variance benchmark; new geometry begins at three overlapping policies.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem verifies that the entire \(Qh+Nu\) treatment-effect fiber and every remaining shape nuisance form a legal local submodel for every finite support with \(L\ge2\); when \(L=2\), the zero-mean shape component correctly has dimension zero.

For every known fixed finite support with \(L\ge2\), two distinct values give the variance floor needed by the jointly measurable deterministic-limit selector. The construction works from any diverging, vanishing-share pilot, stabilizes every fixed nested-cell prefix at nonunique and boundary optima, supplies a schedule- and law-specific spatial rate, and couples the selector to a slowly refining Gaussian rectangle rule.
The upper theorem matches the full-nuisance converse, including for binary outcomes, with an implementable arbitrarily slowly diverging, vanishing-share pilot, a joint estimator, and a terminal rule.
